I've studied biology a fair bit. We are all covered in tiny living things, inside and out. Bacteria, viruses, etc. Being a germophobe is like being afraid of air. I'm not criticizing, just explaining why I no longer fear dirt.

The good news is that only a few of them can make you sick. And most of them die within a few hours on household surfaces. Cloth generally dries them to death in a few minutes.

I'd worry most about bed bugs. They are insects that suck blood and can live for a year without feeding. Bringing them into your house is bad, very bad. Fortunately the heat of a clothes dryer can kill them. Remove the porcelain parts, tie the cloth parts up tight in a pillowcase, then put it in the dryer on high heat for an hour. The innermost parts should get hot enough that if there was a metal button there it would burn your finger.

The porcelain parts can be rinsed in rubbing alcohol and then wiped down with rubbing alcohol. This kills nearly everything that can make you sick.

Seal things in a plastic bag at the thrift store before bringing them home. This keeps bed bugs from migrating to your car or home.
